name: Route Network
description: The node-and-edge graph a transport company is made of: stations and depots as nodes, legs as edges with travel-time estimates, and per-route timetables over the top. It exists because 'expand the network' is the genre's verb and there must be one authoritative answer to 'is there a route from A to B, and when does it run'. This component owns the logical route — stops, order, schedule — not the geometry: actual paths over the world come from movement.pathfinding_system, so a blocked road invalidates a leg through path failure rather than through a second collision model here. Terrain changes arrive as world.tileChanged and world.tileGridBuilt, and a route whose legs no longer path is reported as world.routeBlocked, not silently dropped, because a dead route with vehicles assigned is a decision for utility.depot_dispatch, not a disappearance. It does not own the vehicles that run the routes or the cargo and passengers that ride them; those are dispatch and manifest concerns that read this graph.

inputs.name: maxRoutes
inputs.description: Route cap per company. A real cap forces consolidation decisions late-game instead of letting the map dissolve into spaghetti.

inputs.name: scheduleResolutionMinutes
inputs.description: Timetable granularity in game minutes. Coarser than this and headways stop mattering; finer and schedule editing becomes a spreadsheet job.

inputs.name: autoRelinkOnTileChange
inputs.description: When true, a tile change triggers an immediate path revalidation for affected legs rather than waiting for the next scheduled check.

outputs.name: totalNetworkLength
outputs.description: Summed leg lengths across routes, exposed for score and upkeep calculations.

outputs.name: blockedRouteIds
outputs.description: Routes currently failing path validation. Dispatch and efficiency scoring both read this rather than revalidating.
